item.title: CineSense 2.163.5
item.description:
CineSense 2.163.5

  • When the files on a card are already in the folder (say, after reinstalling), the copy panel now counts steadily up to the end and says "Checking copies already there…" — it no longer flickers between 0 and 1.
  • The finished screen holds still: "Ejecting the card…" is there from the start, and the slow-motion check is one short line that doesn't change the panel's size.
  • A drive that is too full says "Not enough room on <drive>" at the bottom of the panel, and the space it shows is the space that really counts (macOS's "free" includes space it only clears later).
  • In an account that can't change the main Applications folder, CineSense offers to move itself into your own Applications folder instead, and never touches another account's copy.
  • Numbers sit apart: sizes, counts and times are spaced instead of joined by "·", and a count beside a date gets its own small badge.
  • Records: a record in "Needs a look" can be dismissed once you've dealt with it (and brought back); it keeps its red or orange mark in the full list and its log is never changed.
  • The card panel's footer and Preview button no longer shift while it checks, the panel no longer jumps for a frame when it reopens, and CineTransfer's Start never freezes the window while it asks the drives.
  • The steady count also holds for a card that starts by itself before its check is back (auto-ingest, a queue), and CineSync, Settings and CloudSense's test lines keep their numbers apart too.
  • CineTransfer and CloudSense: a service dragged to Destinations shows straight away; Start never does nothing in silence — it starts, or says why; the upload bar never slides backwards; and CloudSense's lists and Records keep their columns apart at any window size (less important columns step aside, the record panel sits beside the list or over it).
  • Settings → Cards: one failed check no longer tells you to retire a card ("often the drive or cable, not the card", with Clear); a pulled drive's run never counts against the card.
  • Records: "Dismiss all" at the top of Needs a look, Dismiss beside Export for one record; the record panel fits its width when you drag the divider; a photos-only "nothing new" record says "16 photos already there".
  • Records: the column headings line up with their columns when scroll bars are always shown, and a day's dash box takes that day's ticks off instead of ticking the rest.
  • The finished screen's CineSearch box keeps one height, and a drive's name never wraps beside its badge.
  • Smaller things: "1 file" and "3 files" instead of "file(s)", an ejected drive in Settings → Advanced is shown by its own name, sizes everywhere read like "2.0 GB", a record of an ingest that copied nothing says "Nothing new — already copied", and a sentence that was cut in the middle now wraps.

item.title: CineSense 2.163.4
item.description:
CineSense 2.163.4

  • Pull a drive out in the middle of a copy and CineSense stops within about a second and says so, plainly: what was copied and checked, what wasn't, and what happened on the card. Nothing you haven't got a checked copy of is ever removed from a card.
  • A Resolve timeline you rename is treated as your edit: later videos go on at its end, and any that were filmed in the middle wait in the day's bin instead of being squeezed in.
  • The card panel says what each drive really needs for this copy, shows "N copied" the moment a card goes in (green once it's proven), and never cuts a drive's name.
  • Records has a calmer list: tick boxes appear when you hover, problem rows have a red or orange edge, numbers line up under their headings, and the footer tells you if something you ticked is scrolled out of view.
  • Reports: clearer names, one kind per report, and you can delete them. A finished copy or ingest now shows a Mac notification as well as the phone ping.
  • Smaller things: one size for a folder everywhere, every linked cloud account offered, a new glass meter for drive space, the CineTransfer window stays in front when you click it, and a slower, smoother light round the search box.

item.title: CineSense 2.140.0
item.description:
CineSense 2.140.0

  • Every Dropbox and Google Drive sign-in asks the service who it is (Dropbox's account id and email, Drive's permissionId and email) and keeps it with the account. The card names it: `you@example.com · CineSense`.
  • Sign in again to a different account is never silent. A dialog names both — "This is a different Dropbox account (new@…) from the one Dropbox was linked to (old@…)" — with Cancel (blue: nothing changes; sign out of Dropbox in the browser first, then Sign in again) or **Use as a New Account** (the old account is unlinked — its History stays, nothing on either account is touched — and the new one is linked and tested).
  • An account linked before 2.140.0 learns who it is the first time Settings → CloudSense is opened (its own token, refreshed with its own client), and its next Sign in again compares with that. **bryzr's Dropbox will read brian@bryzrstudio.com** — the account it is really linked to now; signing in again with the 5.5 TB account asks first.
  • If the service cannot be asked (offline), the sign-in goes through as before, is said as "could not ask which account", and nothing recorded is erased; 2.138.1's size check still speaks after the test.

item.title: CineSense 2.129.2
item.description:
CineSense 2.129.2

  • A linked Dropbox, Google Drive, Backblaze B2 or Amazon S3 account now receives its sign-in or keys. Until this version none of them could connect, whatever you did; a Storage Box was never affected. If you linked one already, press Test again — there is nothing to re-link.

item.title: CineSense 2.129.1
item.description:
CineSense 2.129.1

  • Opening CineSense from Downloads no longer adds a login item for a copy macOS deletes on restart. It starts at login once it is in your Applications folder — and if you choose "Not Now" on the move offer, it now says so.
  • Click the CineSense icon in the menu bar for its menu; right-click it for the ingest panel (it was the other way round). The panel still appears by itself when a card goes in, and stays in the menu as Ingest Panel.
  • CloudSense's panel: two clear icons switch between the big card and the compact list, a bigger gear opens its settings, and "Stay awake" (a moon and a switch) sits alone at the bottom. Clicking the upload line in the menu always opens the big card.
  • A single large video uploads over one connection to a Storage Box or SFTP server, so a day of one big file goes slower than a day of many. The panel now says so when it happens, and Test connection shows that one-connection speed and what a single 100 GB file would take.
  • Copy Diagnostics reports memory the way About This Mac does (a 64 GB Mac says 64 GB).

item.title: CineSense 2.129.0
item.description:
CineSense 2.129.0

  • CineSense is now signed by Bryzr Studio and notarised by Apple: open it and macOS asks only the usual "downloaded from the internet — Open?". No Terminal commands, no System Settings detour.
  • Opened from Downloads, CineSense offers to move itself into Applications, where it starts at login and updates install.
  • Updates come by themselves: CineSense checks once a day, and a new version is a line at the top of its menu — nothing pops up. An update never installs while a card, a transfer or an upload is in progress; it waits, then CineSense relaunches by itself. Settings → About → Check for Updates checks now, and "Receive beta updates" offers test versions first.
  • Something went wrong? Menu → Copy Diagnostics shows exactly what it will gather, can hide your card and folder names, and puts it all in a folder in Downloads for you to email to beta@bryzrstudio.com. CineSense never sends anything itself, and never includes footage, passwords or keys.
